name: Plant Hopper
tagline: A turret that finds each plant with a camera and shoots it exactly the water it needs, controlled from a web app.
problem: Sprinklers water every plant the same way on the same schedule, and the team cites up to half of that water being wasted.
solution: A two-axis turret locates each plant by its fiducial tag, computes distance and offset, aligns with a PID loop and trigonometry, and fires a servo-controlled water gun. Soil-moisture readings and camera images go to a cloud database; a web app shows plant health and sends commands such as water now or scan, which a multithreaded Python controller executes on the hardware.
demo_moment: Team-described: press water now in the web app and the turret turns to the right plant and waters it.

why_it_stood_out.claim: Took first place overall among 124 submissions.
Opens with a single number about wasted water and promises a measurable fix.
Integrates custom CAD hardware, tag-based vision, PID aiming, a cloud database and a web app in one weekend.
A turret that shoots water at plants is a physical demo judges remember, and the web app shows it is more than a toy.

lessons: Pair a playful physical action with one hard number about the problem; the number makes the toy credible.
